title: The Campfire
description: Pierre shares a story from Arcole. The night before Rivoli.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: The campfire crackles in the January cold. Three men sit around it — close enough for warmth, far enough for pride. The mountains are black against the stars.

pierre_1.speaker: pierre
pierre_1.text: Arcole was different. We crossed a bridge under fire — *seventy-five paces* of open causeway, Austrian grapeshot the whole way. Men fell like wheat.

pierre_inner.speaker: pierre
pierre_inner.text: He's seeing it again. The bridge. The dead. You can tell by the way his eyes go distant.

pierre_2.speaker: pierre
pierre_2.text: I didn't think about surviving. I thought about the man in front of me. When he fell, I stepped over him and kept walking. That's all there is.

player_choice_1.speaker: narrator
player_choice_1.text: The fire pops. Sparks spiral upward into the dark. Pierre stares into the flames. Jean-Baptiste looks at you.

choices.label: "Were you afraid?"
choices.description: Ask the question JB wants answered.

choices.label: Say nothing. Stare into the fire.

bonaparte_branch.speaker: pierre
bonaparte_branch.text: He grabbed the flag **himself**. Ran onto the bridge. Aides falling around him. _Madness_ — or genius. I still don't know which. But every man who saw it followed him.

fear_branch.speaker: pierre
fear_branch.text: Every second. But fear is like the cold — you can *feel* it and still keep moving. The trick is not to think. Just put **one foot in front of the other**.

silence_branch.speaker: narrator
silence_branch.text: You say nothing. Pierre glances at you — a flicker of something that might be respect. The fire crackles. Jean-Baptiste watches both of you, trying to learn the language of soldiers who have survived.

jb_react_1.speaker: jb
jb_react_1.text: Bonaparte himself? On the bridge? They... they don't mention that in the dispatches.

pierre_end_1.speaker: pierre
pierre_end_1.text: The dispatches mention what Paris needs to hear. Not what the bridge looked like after.

jb_react_2.speaker: jb
jb_react_2.text: One foot in front of the other...

pierre_end_2.speaker: pierre
pierre_end_2.text: Get some sleep, both of you. Tomorrow we find out if the advice is worth anything.

ending.speaker: narrator
ending.text: The fire burns lower. One by one, the campfires across the plateau wink out. Tomorrow, the Austrians come. Tonight, three men share warmth and silence.

title: Felix's Card Trick
description: Felix Martel entertains the garrison with sleight of hand. Voltri camp.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: Evening in the garrison. Felix Martel sits cross-legged on a barrel, a battered deck of cards appearing and disappearing between his fingers like small miracles.

felix_1.speaker: felix
felix_1.text: Pick a card. Any card. Don't show me — I already know what it is. That's the trick. Not the card. The knowing.

morin_1.speaker: morin
morin_1.text: Martel, if you spent half as much time cleaning your musket as you do shuffling those damn cards...

felix_2.speaker: felix
felix_2.text: Sergeant, my musket fires just fine. The cards, on the other hand, require daily practice. A man has priorities.

player_choice.speaker: narrator
player_choice.text: Felix fans the deck toward you with a showman's flourish.

choices.label: "Cards won't stop an Austrian musket ball."

pick_card.speaker: felix
pick_card.text: The seven of hearts. Don't look surprised — I told you, the knowing is the trick. In the theatre, they called it "reading the room." In the army, they call it "not getting shot." Same skill, different stage.

backstory.speaker: felix
backstory.text: I was a travelling player. Commedia dell'arte, mostly. Before the Revolution ate the theatres. Turns out a man who can make a crowd laugh can also make a squad follow orders — if he phrases them right.

morin_react.speaker: morin
morin_react.text: That explains the dramatics. And the insubordination.

felix_laugh.speaker: felix
felix_laugh.text: Sergeant, in the theatre, insubordination is called 'improvisation.' Much better word.

serious.speaker: felix
serious.text: No. They won't. Nothing stops a musket ball except another body, and I'd rather not be that body. So I shuffle cards. It keeps my hands *steady*. Steady hands, steady nerve. **That's** what the cards are for.

end_light.speaker: narrator
end_light.text: Felix palms the deck and makes it vanish into his coat. Sergeant Morin shakes his head, but you catch the ghost of a smile before he turns away.

end_serious.speaker: narrator
end_serious.text: Felix puts the cards away. For a moment, the mask slips — and behind the showman is just another scared man in a uniform. Then the grin returns. "Another game, perhaps? No? Suit yourself."

title: Duval's Inspection
description: Sergeant Duval inspects your kit. Pre-battle tension.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: First light. The camp stirs with the mechanical ritual of an army preparing for battle. Sergeant Duval moves through the section like a storm front.

narrator_1.speaker: narrator
narrator_1.text: He snatches your musket, checks the flint, peers down the barrel, tests the bayonet socket. His movements are fast and sure — a man who has done this a thousand times.

confident.speaker: duval
confident.text: I'll decide what's clean, Private. Your opinion on the matter is not required.

duval_inspect_2.speaker: narrator
duval_inspect_2.text: He hands the musket back. His eyes move to the next man. You passed — barely.

challenge.speaker: duval
challenge.text: The problem, Private, is that in three hours you'll be shooting at men who want to kill you, and if this flint doesn't spark, they will succeed. Any other questions?

transition.speaker: narrator
transition.text: Captain Leclerc appears at the end of the line. Duval straightens imperceptibly.

duval_report.speaker: duval
duval_report.text: Ready as they'll ever be, Captain. Flints good. Cartridges counted. They'll hold.

leclerc_2.speaker: leclerc
leclerc_2.text: Good. The drums beat in thirty minutes. Make sure every man has eaten.

ending.speaker: narrator
ending.text: Leclerc moves on. Duval watches him go, then turns back to the section. "You heard the captain. Eat something. It may be your last chance." It is unclear if he means the meal or the chance.

title: The Bridge at Lodi
description: In the aftermath of the charge, a moment of reckoning on the bridge.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: Smoke drifts across the bridge like a funeral shroud. The Austrian guns are silent now. Bodies lie where they fell — French and Austrian tangled together, impossible to tell apart in death.

duval_1.speaker: duval
duval_1.text: Check the wounded. French first, then Austrian. Anyone who can walk, get them off this bridge before the engineers come through.

pierre_1.speaker: pierre
pierre_1.text: Twelve guns. We charged twelve guns across an open bridge. The textbooks will call it brilliant. I call it luck.

narrator_1.speaker: narrator
narrator_1.text: A wounded Austrian officer lies propped against the bridge railing, clutching his side. He watches you approach with eyes that expect the worst.

choice_1.speaker: narrator
choice_1.text: The officer's sword lies beside him. He makes no move for it.

choices.label: Take his sword as a trophy.
Walk past. There are French wounded first.

mercy.speaker: narrator
mercy.text: You kneel and hold the canteen to his lips. He drinks, coughs, drinks again. "Danke," he whispers. Pierre watches from the railing. Something shifts in his expression — not quite approval. Recognition.

trophy.speaker: duval
trophy.text: Leave it. He's an officer — that sword gets turned in to the captain, not stuffed in your kit. We're soldiers, not looters.

duty.speaker: pierre
duty.text: You're learning. The French wounded can't wait while you play at mercy. Tend your own first. Then, if there's time...

duval_react.speaker: duval
duval_react.text: Move it. We hold this bridge until the column crosses. After that, you can philosophise all you want.

ending.speaker: narrator
ending.text: The column begins to cross — thousands of boots on stone, the army pouring south like a river finding its course. You stand on a bridge that will be famous. Right now, it just smells of powder and blood.

title: The Mountain Pass
description: Crossing the Alps in winter. The army struggles through snow and silence.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: The pass narrows to a track barely wide enough for two men abreast. Below, a gorge drops into white nothing. Above, the peaks vanish into cloud. The army moves in single file, breathing frost.

jb_1.speaker: jb
jb_1.text: I can't feel my feet. Is that... is that normal? Should I be worried about that?

felix_1.speaker: felix
felix_1.text: Worried? In the theatre, we called that 'dedication to the role.' You're playing a frozen soldier. Magnificently, I might add.

jb_2.speaker: jb
jb_2.text: Felix, I'm serious. What if we don't make it across?

felix_2.speaker: felix
felix_2.text: Then we become very picturesque statues and future travellers will wonder who we were. But that won't happen. You know why?

choices.label: "Because Felix would talk the mountain into moving."
"Because we have to. There's no going back."

joke.speaker: felix
joke.text: Ha! I once convinced a Parisian landlord that I'd already paid rent for three months. A mountain should be easier — it can't argue back.

jb_laugh.speaker: jb
jb_laugh.text: You're mad. Both of you. Completely mad.

resolve.speaker: felix
resolve.text: Exactly. The road only goes forward. That's the secret the generals don't tell you — courage isn't a choice when there's no alternative.

silence.speaker: narrator
silence.text: You say nothing. Felix nods — he understands. The three of you walk on, boots crunching in snow, breath hanging in the air like small ghosts. Sometimes company is enough.

ending.speaker: narrator
ending.text: The path begins to descend. Through a gap in the clouds, Italy appears below — green and gold and impossibly warm. The whole column stops. For a moment, no one speaks. Then someone — you never learn who — starts to sing.

title: The Gorge
description: Trapped in a ravine. Austrian Grenzer above. Decisions under fire.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: The gorge closes around the column like a fist. Cliff walls rise on both sides — bare rock, grey and wet. The sound of water echoes from somewhere below. Then the first shot cracks from above.

morin_1.speaker: morin
morin_1.text: Grenzer! On the ridgeline! Get against the wall — NOW!

narrator_1.speaker: narrator
narrator_1.text: Shots crack and echo between the cliffs, impossible to tell direction from the ricochets. A man three paces behind you falls without a sound. The column bunches against the rock wall like cattle in a storm.

pierre_1.speaker: pierre
pierre_1.text: We're fish in a barrel. They don't even need to aim — just fire into the mass and God does the rest.

morin_2.speaker: morin
morin_2.text: Stow it, Private! I need solutions, not sermons. There — that goat path. If we can get a squad up the left face, we can flank them.

choice_1.speaker: narrator
choice_1.text: Morin looks at you. The goat path is barely visible — loose scree and a handful of scrub brush for cover. The Grenzer fire steadily from above.

choices.label: "I'll go, Sergeant."
choices.description: Volunteer for the climb. Dangerous but decisive.

choices.label: "Send Pierre — he's done this before."
choices.description: Pierre survived Arcole. He can survive this.

choices.label: "We should wait for artillery."
choices.description: The guns are coming. Patience over bravery.

volunteer.speaker: morin
volunteer.text: Good man. Take four others. Keep low. Don't fire until you're level with them — surprise is the only advantage you'll have. Go.

deflect.speaker: pierre
deflect.text: He's right. I'll go. But remember this — next time, it's your turn to climb.

wait.speaker: morin
wait.text: Artillery? In a gorge? Use your head, soldier! The guns can't elevate enough. We solve this ourselves or we die here. Pierre — you're going up. Move!

climb.speaker: narrator
climb.text: The climbing party scrambles up the goat path, rocks clattering beneath their feet. Below, Morin keeps the column pressed against the wall, returning sporadic fire. Minutes pass like hours. Then — a volley from above, and the Grenzer fire stops. Shouts in German, then silence.

aftermath.speaker: morin
aftermath.text: Move! Before they regroup! Double time through the gorge — we stop for nothing!

ending.speaker: narrator
ending.text: The column surges forward, stepping over the fallen, boots splashing through the stream. The gorge opens ahead — sunlight and open ground. Behind you, the cliffs hold their silence and their dead.

title: The March South
description: The army descends from the Alps into Italy. Hope and exhaustion.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: The road winds down from the pass like a white ribbon. Below, the Piedmontese plain stretches to the horizon — farmland, vineyards, church steeples. After weeks of mountain cold, the warmth feels like forgiveness.

jb_1.speaker: jb
jb_1.text: Look at it! Green fields, real trees... is that a vineyard? Please tell me that's a vineyard.

felix_1.speaker: felix
felix_1.text: It is. And those are olive trees. And that — unless my nose deceives me — is bread baking somewhere in that village. Real bread. Not the stone they've been feeding us.

morin_1.speaker: morin
morin_1.text: Don't get comfortable. We're not here for the wine. The Piedmontese army is three days' march ahead. Enjoy the view while walking.

jb_2.speaker: jb
jb_2.text: My feet are bleeding. Both of them. The left shoe lost its sole somewhere above the snow line.

choice_1.speaker: narrator
choice_1.text: Jean-Baptiste limps on, his face drawn tight. Felix walks in theatrical silence, conserving energy for the first audience he can find. Morin keeps pace at the rear, watching for stragglers.

choices.label: Give JB your spare stockings.
choices.description: You packed an extra pair. He needs them more.

choices.label: "Sing something, Felix."
choices.description: The column could use a lift.

choices.label: March in silence. Save your strength.
choices.description: Italy will arrive when it arrives.

kindness.speaker: jb
kindness.text: You... are you sure? These are — thank you. I won't forget this.

song.speaker: felix
song.text: I thought you'd never ask! Allons enfants de la patrie—

morin_react_2.speaker: morin
morin_react_2.text: Something quieter, Martel. We're not on stage.

felix_2.speaker: felix
felix_2.text: Fine. Something for the road, then.

morin_react.speaker: morin
morin_react.text: Keep up, both of you. Generosity doesn't excuse tardiness.

silent_march.speaker: narrator
silent_march.text: You march. The sun warms your back. The road turns south and the mountains shrink behind you. Jean-Baptiste limps, Felix hums under his breath, Morin watches everything. The army moves like a single organism — tired, hungry, unstoppable.

ending.speaker: narrator
ending.text: By evening, the column reaches the valley floor. Cook fires bloom across the fields like scattered stars. The mountains are a dark wall behind you. Ahead, Italy waits — beautiful and unsuspecting. Tomorrow, the campaign begins in earnest.

title: The Passe-Dix Game
description: Felix Martel runs the table behind the cookfires.

intro_1.speaker: narrator
intro_1.text: Evening. A knot of soldiers crowds around a blanket spread in the dirt behind the cookfires. Dice clatter. Coins change hands.

intro_2.speaker: narrator
intro_2.text: In the middle of it all sits a man you’ve seen around camp — Felix Martel, a former musician with quick hands and a quicker smile. He’s running the table and enjoying every minute.

felix_invite.speaker: felix
felix_invite.text: "Room for one more, friend. Two sous to play. The dice don’t care about rank."

choices.label: Join the game
choices.description: Sit down, put your money in, roll the dice.

choices.label: Watch
choices.description: Stand at the edge. Learn how Felix works before risking your money.

choices.label: Decline
choices.description: Walk away. You didn’t survive this long by gambling.

empty_purse.speaker: narrator
empty_purse.text: You reach for your purse and find it empty.

empty_end.speaker: narrator
empty_end.text: The game goes on without you.

join_sit.speaker: narrator
join_sit.text: You sit down and put your sous in the pot. Felix grins and hands you the dice.

dice_roll.speaker: felix
dice_roll.text: "Let’s see what fortune thinks of you."

win_1.speaker: narrator
win_1.text: The dice tumble and settle. The crowd leans in. A murmur of approval.

win_2.speaker: narrator
win_2.text: The dice are kind tonight — or maybe Felix lets you win. You walk away with heavier pockets and a new acquaintance.

lose_1.speaker: narrator
lose_1.text: The dice tumble and settle. Felix already has that look — the one that says he knew exactly how they’d fall.

lose_2.speaker: narrator
lose_2.text: You watch your sous disappear. You walk away lighter in the purse but richer in understanding: never trust a musician with dice.

watch_1.speaker: narrator
watch_1.text: You stand at the edge and watch Felix work. He’s good — quick hands, easy patter, always knows when to let someone win just enough to keep them playing.

watch_2.speaker: felix
watch_2.text: He catches your eye once and winks.

watch_end.speaker: narrator
watch_end.text: You file the observation away for later.

decline_1.speaker: narrator
decline_1.text: You shake your head and walk on.

decline_end.speaker: narrator
decline_end.text: The dice rattle behind you as you go.

converge.speaker: narrator
converge.text: The game breaks up as the night deepens. Felix pockets his winnings with practiced ease and melts back into the camp.
